stem.text: Which description of movement of substances during tissue fluid formation is correct?

A.text: Low hydrostatic pressure forces substances out of the capillary at the arterial end allowing small substances to enter the fluid that bathes the cells.

B.text: Tissue fluid moves back into the venule due to a net hydrostatic pressure change in the capillary.

C.text: Movement of water in tissue fluid into the capillary by osmosis is due to the low water potential and low hydrostatic pressure inside the capillary.

D.text: A high water potential of the surrounding tissue fluid causes substances to leave the capillaries at the arterial end.
